$description:
Praxis — one theme, dark by default with a light appearance.

Collapsed on 2026-10-03 from two themes in the platform: claude-like, which supplied everything structural (ground, surfaces, type scale, the shape of every control), and praxis, which supplied the accent, the logos and the mark. There is no longer a separate parent; what follows is both.

— From claude-like —

Claude-like theme — the Business User concept.

A deliberate opposite to a printed-document theme:
squared corners, rules instead of shadows, dense small type, ink on paper.
This is an application surface, and a dark one — taken from the Claude
desktop app rather than from a print deck.

Measured off a screenshot of the real thing rather than guessed:
ground          warm charcoal, never a blue-grey
sidebar         a shade darker than the working area, not lighter
type            off-white, and the greeting is a serif at display size
accent          the coral of the Claude mark, used once per screen
controls        low-contrast fills; the active one is lighter, not coloured

The restraint is the point. Almost nothing on that screen carries a colour,
and what a control does is said with an icon rather than a word, so the only
saturated thing in view is the mark itself.

Same token contract as the other two themes, so ui.css never learns which
one is on.

— From praxis —

Praxis.

A member of the conversational family, so everything structural — the near
black ground, the surfaces, the type scale, the shape of every control —
comes from `[data-family="conversational"]` in claude-like.css. What is
declared here is only what makes this theme Praxis: its red, its logo, its
mark, and the line of provenance in the corner.

The highlight is the warm tip of the mark's gradient rather than its red
body. The red covers far more of the artwork — it is what the tool picks on
coverage alone — but the reddish-orange is the colour the mark is going
towards, and it was chosen deliberately over the measurement.

#FF6642, hue 11, the most prevalent of the seventy warm shades that make up
the gradient's tip. It is used as TEXT in the kickers above every answer, so
it is fitted to each ground rather than used raw: it clears 4.5:1 untouched
on the dark ground, and has to travel 22% darker to clear it on the light
one. That second move is large — the hue survives but the orange reads much
deeper — and it is the honest cost of a colour this light on a pale ground.

Logos are drawn as supplied rather than painted, because the mark carries
two colours and a gradient that a stencil would flatten to one. That is why
there are two of them: dark ink for the light ground, light ink for the
dark one.

A note on the file names they arrived with. `praxis-dark.png` is dark INK,
for a LIGHT ground; `powered-by-dark.png` is for a DARK ground. Two opposite
conventions in one folder, which is why the copies here are named for the
ground they sit on and nothing else.
name: praxis
title: Praxis

accent.$description: the warm tip of the mark, as it stands

ground.$description: the working ground — near-black, still warm

ground-recessed.$description:
the rail: a shelf BEHIND the work,
so it is darker than the ground

on-accent.$description: Text and counts drawn on the accent (was the literal value of --badge-fg).

structure.$description: the structural role; light here, not blue

surface.$description: composer, cards — lifted off the ground

text-subtle.$description: Lifted from the platform's #7E7A72 to clear 4.5:1 on paper, surface and the sunken panel (5.05, 4.56, 4.78).

live.$description:
Optional. Set --favicon to a url() to supply one; leave it out and the
app draws one from the brand mark in this theme's --logo-paint, which is
why adding a theme never means remembering to draw an icon.
See web/favicon.js.

Availability, dimmed to sit on a dark ground without glowing.

logo-paint.$description: the tab icon, where the mark is painted flat

logo-image.$description:
The wordmark, drawn as supplied (v2, 2026-10-07: praxis-v2-light.svg and praxis-v2-dark.svg, framed to the artwork's drawn bounds plus 8 units).

The aspect is set per appearance because the two files are not quite the same
shape — 3.029 and 3.045. Using one ratio for both letterboxes one of them.

logo-height.$description:
A third larger than the default 28px. This artwork is a mark plus a
wordmark where the shared default was sized for a wordmark alone, so the
letters come out smaller at the same height.

mark-image.$description: The mark: beside the greeting, and in the tab (v2, 2026-10-07: praxis-v2-favicon.svg, framed to its drawn bounds). Square.

accent.$description: the same hue, 22% deeper to read on pale

ground-recessed.$description:
Same relationship in daylight: a shade deeper than the working
ground, not a white card floating on it.

on-accent.$description: Text and counts drawn on the accent (was the literal value of --badge-fg).

text-subtle.$description: Darkened from the platform's #8F8A7E to clear 4.5:1 on paper (4.51); this close to --muted, light has one quiet text tier, not two.

limited.$description: Darkened a step from the platform's #9A6B24 to clear 4.5:1 on the sunken panel (4.51).

evaluation.$description: Darkened a step from the platform's #7A756A to clear 4.5:1 on the sunken panel (4.54).

A third larger than the default 28px. This artwork is a mark plus a
wordmark where the shared default was sized for a wordmark alone, so the
